mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the CPIAUCSL index above 250.5 in the next month signals rising inflation expectations, triggering market stress and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 250.5 in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not turn negative within 30 days of the CPIAUCSL crossing above 250.5, or the effect persists beyond the initial stress period.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent low federal funds rates and rising demand (GDPC1) create a favorable macro environment, amplifying equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect between FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 does not predict significant positive returns in 20-day windows where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in RSAFS demand metrics below 500 million in the next month during a late-cycle expansion signals weakening demand, prompting market adjustments that result in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below 500 in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not turn negative within 30 days of RSAFS falling below 500 during a late-cycle expansion regime.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment rates (UNRATE) combined with rising demand (HOUST) create a dual supportive environment, enhancing corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The combined effect of UNRATE and HOUST does not correlate with statistically significant positive returns in 20-day windows where both series meet their respective conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in supply metrics (INDPRO falling below 100) indicates weakening production capacity, which may lead to price pressures and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as markets anticipate inflation.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 100 in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not turn positive within 30 days of INDPRO falling below 100, or the effect is short-lived and fades within the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a rise in the federal funds rate above 1.8% signals tighter policy, raising borrowing costs and dampening equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.8% in the next month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not turn negative within 90 days of FEDFUNDS crossing above 1.8% during a tightening cycle, or the effect is not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: An upward trend in quarterly demand (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity, boosting corporate profits and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns do not turn positive within 10 days of GDPC1 showing an upward trend, or the effect is not immediate.
